en.p: As shown in the figure, there is a sheet of paper shaped like a square ABCD with side length 8, with two semicircles attached whose diameters are the segments AB and CD, respectively. Let P be the point closer to B among the points dividing the arc AB of the semicircle into three equal parts, and let Q be the point bisecting the arc CD of the semicircle.

When the two semicircles are folded up along the segments AB and CD as fold lines, let G, H be the feet of the perpendiculars from the two points P, Q to the plane ABCD, respectively; then the two points G, H lie inside the square ABCD, and $\overline{\mathrm{PG}}=\sqrt{3}$, $\overline{\mathrm{QH}}=2\sqrt{3}$. When $\theta$ is the angle between the two planes PCQ and ABCD, find the value of $70\times\cos^2\theta$. (Ignore the thickness of the paper.) [4 points]
